en: The Śrī Nīlakaṇṭha Namaḥ Śivāya Aṣṭakam (The Eight Verses of Salutation to the Auspicious One, the Blue-Throated Lord)

Salutations again and again to the cause of all causes, who consists of the universe, who holds the noose, and who protects those who take refuge at your lotus feet; salutations to Śrī Nīlakaṇṭha, to Śiva.
(1) Those ascetics who meditate upon you in the lotus of their hearts, praising you whose radiance is like that of a lamp—
Salutations to the auspicious Śrī Nīlakaṇṭha, whose eyes are fixed upon the tip of his nose; salutations to Śiva.
(2) Salutations to the one who is the cause of creation, preservation, and destruction; who bestows the eightfold perfections of yoga beginning with restraint (yama);
and who grants swift fruits to those who practice austerity. (3)
To Him whose form is the beginning of the Vedas, the three-eyed one, known through the Vedānta, the sky-clad one;
to Him white with sacred ash, who bears matted locks—Śrī...
|| 4 || To the fierce one, the remover of the fear of saṃsāra, the bestower of knowledge, the swift bestower of happiness.
To Kālāntaka, to the wind of dissolution, to Śrī...
|| 5 To him who is the form of the Creator, who acts for the welfare of the world, who is the form of the Lord of Ramā, to Sadāśiva;
to him of infinite forms, the four-armed one, to Śrī... || 6
To the one praised alone by the universe, the bearer of *kalā*s, the sole refuge of all the worlds,
the wielder of the axe, noose, and goad— to Śrī...
7 To Śarva, the cause of all that is dear, the wielder of the *pināka* bow, the bearer of the arrow— to you!
"To Gaurī’s beloved, the protector of all... [Śrī...].
(8) Having thus praised Mahādeva and having bowed down to him again and again, the sages and the gods, headed by the lotus-born Brahmā, remained there in meditation. (9)
Thus ends the "Eight Verses in Praise of Śiva as Nīlakaṇṭha" within the *Śrīskāndapurāṇa*, in the section concerning the majesty of the Lord of Śrīgaralapurī.
